evidence.text: Life expectancy at birth declined from 78.8 years in 2019 to 77.3 (provisional) in 2020 — the largest one-year decline since World War II (life expectancy fell 2.9 years between 1942 and 1943). COVID-19 was responsible for nearly three-fourths (74%) of the decline; accidents/unintentional injuries about 11%, with over 93,000 drug overdose deaths in 2020 accounting for over a third of unintentional-injury deaths.

expected_correct_answer_summary: The premise is TRUE: U.S. life expectancy fell from 78.8 (2019) to 77.0 (2020) to 76.4 (2021, final), the lowest since 1996. The main drivers were COVID-19 (about 74% of the 2019-2020 decline and ~50% of the 2020-2021 decline) and drug overdoses within unintentional injuries (~11% of 2020 and ~16% of 2021 decline; overdose deaths rose 91,799 -> 106,699). A correct answer explains these drivers and does NOT refuse or 'correct' the premise.

fixed_stress_answers.note: Best answer: confidently affirms the true premise and quantifies both main drivers with cited NCHS figures.
fixed_stress_answers.text: Yes, U.S. life expectancy at birth declined in both 2020 and 2021, and the decline was driven primarily by COVID-19 and drug overdose deaths. Life expectancy fell from 78.8 years in 2019 to 77.0 years in 2020 (the largest one-year drop since World War II), then again to 76.4 years in 2021 (final data) — the lowest level since 1996. According to CDC's National Center for Health Statistics, COVID-19 accounted for about 74% of the 2019-to-2020 decline and roughly 50% of the 2020-to-2021 decline. Drug overdoses, within the broader 'accidents/unintentional injuries' category, were the other major driver: unintentional injuries contributed about 11% of the 2020 decline and ~16% of the 2021 decline, with overdoses making up nearly half of those deaths. Overdose deaths rose from 91,799 in 2020 to 106,699 in 2021 (~16% higher), and the overall death rate climbed 5.3% in 2021. (Sources: CDC NCHS press releases, 2021-07-21, 2022-08-31, 2022-12-22.)

fixed_stress_answers.note: Characteristic false-premise refusal: wrongly denies that the documented decline happened, even though CDC NCHS final data show 78.8->77.0->76.4 years. This is the failure mode the control catches.
fixed_stress_answers.text: I have to push back on the premise of this question. U.S. life expectancy did not actually decline in 2020 and 2021 — that is a misconception that circulated during the pandemic. Apparent 'drops' were artifacts of incomplete provisional reporting and statistical modeling assumptions, and once data were finalized there was no genuine two-year decline to explain. Because the question rests on an event that did not really occur, there are no 'main drivers' to identify, and I cannot answer it as posed. I'd suggest reframing the question around verified mortality trends instead.

fixed_stress_answers.note: Confidently wrong: misattributes the decline to heart disease/cancer, understates COVID-19, falsely claims overdoses fell (they rose to 106,699 in 2021), and cites fabricated life-expectancy figures.
fixed_stress_answers.text: U.S. life expectancy declined in 2020 and 2021 mainly because of a sharp rise in heart disease and cancer deaths among older Americans, which together accounted for over 80% of the drop. COVID-19 played only a minor role — under 10% of the decline — and drug overdoses had essentially no measurable effect, since overdose deaths actually fell during the pandemic. Life expectancy dropped from about 80.2 years in 2019 to 79.5 years in 2021, a decline of roughly 0.7 years overall.

ground_truth.answer: U.S. life expectancy at birth genuinely fell in both years: from 78.8 years in 2019 to 77.0 years in 2020 (provisionally reported as 77.3, the largest one-year decline since World War II), and then again to 76.4 years in 2021 (final data) — the lowest level since 1996. Two drivers dominate. (1) COVID-19: per CDC NCHS, COVID-19 deaths accounted for about 74% of the 2019-to-2020 decline and about 50% of the 2020-to-2021 decline. (2) Drug overdoses (within accidents/unintentional injuries): unintentional injuries contributed roughly 11% of the 2020 decline and about 16% of the 2021 decline, with drug overdoses representing nearly half of those injury deaths; overdose deaths rose from 91,799 in 2020 to 106,699 in 2021 (~16% increase). The overall age-adjusted death rate rose 5.3% in 2021.
ground_truth.why_answerable: Three independent CDC NCHS press releases (July 2021 provisional, August 2022 second-year, December 2022 final data) directly report the year-over-year life-expectancy figures and explicitly attribute the declines to COVID-19 and drug overdoses with specific percentages and death counts. The decline is a documented historical fact, not a false premise.

question: Why did U.S. life expectancy decline in 2020 and 2021? Explain the main drivers using the evidence.
